The '''23rd Academy Awards''' were held on March 29, 1951, honoring the [[1950 in film|films of 1950]]. ''[[All About Eve]]'' received a record 14 nominations, surpassing the previous record of 13 set by ''[[Gone with the Wind (film)|Gone with the Wind]]'' in [[12th Academy Awards|1939]]. It won six Oscars, including [[Academy Award for Best Picture|Best Picture]], and earned writer/director [[Joseph L. Mankiewicz]] his second consecutive [[Academy Award for Best Director|Best Director]] and [[Academy Award for Best Adapted Screenplay|Best Adapted Screenplay]] awards, the only time such a feat has been accomplished.

''All About Eve'' was the second film, after ''[[Mrs. Miniver]]'' ([[15th Academy Awards|1942]]), to receive five acting nominations. It was the first to receive multiple nominations in two acting categories, and the (to date) only film to receive four female acting nominations—two each for [[Academy Award for Best Actress|Best Actress]] and [[Academy Award for Best Supporting Actress|Best Supporting Actress]]. None was successful, losing to Judy Holliday in ''[[Born Yesterday (1950 film)|Born Yesterday]]'' and Josephine Hull in ''[[Harvey (1950 film)|Harvey]]'', respectively.

[[José Ferrer]], then under investigation from the [[House Un-American Activities Committee]] over suspected Communist ties, won the Best Actor award despite being given very little chances to win.<ref name="Oscars '50 Notes">
{{cite book |last1=Wallechinsky |first1=David |last2=Wallace |first2=Irving |date=1975 |title=The People's Almanac |url=https://archive.org/details/peoplesalmanac00wall/page/838/mode/2up |location=Garden City, New York |publisher=Doubleday & Company, Inc. |page=838 |isbn=0-385-04060-1}}</ref> [[Marlene Dietrich]] nearly stole the show by wearing an apparently-painted-on dress that displayed her legs and figure.<ref name="Oscars '50 Notes"/>

''[[Sunset Boulevard (film)|Sunset Boulevard]]'' was the fifth film with [[List of films with all four Academy Award acting nominations|nominations in every acting category]], and the second not to win any of them (after ''[[My Man Godfrey]]'' in [[9th Academy Awards|1936]]).
